author.name: Boyo Martínez
author.bio: Boyo leads product and design at NicaSource, where he helps US companies plan, staff and run nearshore engineering teams. He has spent fifteen years shipping digital products with distributed teams across the Americas.

meta.body:
Introduction

For East Coast companies, Central America sits one or two hours behind New York, depending on the season. That small offset is one of the most underrated advantages in nearshore staffing.

The Shape of an Eastern Day

Morning alignment

Your product managers set priorities first thing; by the time your nearshore engineers sign on, the backlog is groomed and the questions are written down.

Evening coverage

The nearshore team keeps working after the New York office winds down, which gives you a natural window for deploys, monitoring and support without anyone pulling a night shift.

What to Watch For

  • Daylight saving changes shift the overlap twice a year; put them on the shared calendar.
  • Agree on a hard stop for meetings so the late hour stays focused.

Conclusion

An Eastern client with a Central American team gets almost total overlap plus an extra hour of runway every day. Plan around it and it becomes a competitive edge.
